questions.question: A VPNv4 route is reflected but its next hop remains an unreachable PE. Which control targets that address family?

options.text: Enable next-hop-self on all unicast peers.
options.feedback: This affects ordinary next-hop behavior, not VPNv4 route reflection.

options.text: Enable next-hop-self-rr-vpnv4 for the RR client.
options.feedback: Correct: the AF-specific RR setting rewrites VPNv4 NEXT_HOP.
Route targets control VPN membership, not the transport next hop.
Redistribution changes route sources and may leak routes; it does not rewrite the reflected attribute.

questions.question: A whole PE group needs VPNv6 next-hop rewriting, while other clients stay unchanged. Where should the setting live?

options.feedback: A global change is broader than the intended peer population.
A static route may restore reachability but does not implement the RR attribute policy.
Correct: neighbor-group scope applies the rewrite only to that client set.
Route-targets decide route membership, not NEXT_HOP rewriting.

questions.question: The BGP session is Established and the VPN route is present, but forwarding fails. What evidence best separates receipt from usability?

options.text: Inspect the installed gateway and recursive resolution.
options.feedback: Correct: the routing table and recursive lookup show whether the next hop can forward.
Uptime proves session stability, not a usable FIB entry.
RT configuration matters if the route is absent; the route is already present.
Administrator history does not explain next-hop resolution.

questions.question: After enabling VPNv4 next-hop-self, the route is still absent from the VPN table. What should be checked first?

options.feedback: Wireless link state is unrelated to VPN route distribution.
The SASE key controls management registration.
SAML digest controls admin login.
Correct: absent VPN NLRI points to RT policy or address-family activation before next-hop troubleshooting.

questions.question: FMG and SASE use different FortiCare accounts but valid parent/child OU placement. What is needed?

options.feedback: A FortiGate password does not authorize SASE registration.

options.text: A FortiManager Key from SASE Central Management Settings.
options.feedback: Correct: generate and provide the tenant FortiManager Key when accounts differ.
The Global Database ADOM is not a supported destination.
FortiAnalyzer licensing is unrelated to the connector key.

questions.question: Adding SASE fails because the selected ADOM is in Backup mode. What is the correction?

options.feedback: Correct: FortiSASE cannot be added to a Backup-mode ADOM.
Revoking keys removes authorization rather than fixing ADOM mode.
Global Database is also unsupported.
The VDOM name does not change ADOM eligibility.

questions.question: A synchronized object was deleted from FMG and the SASE tenant now conflicts. Which rule was ignored?

options.text: SAML endpoints must share a digest.
options.feedback: SAML settings do not govern configuration synchronization.
MLO is a wireless capability.

options.text: Central sync is one-way from FMG to SASE.
options.feedback: Correct: FortiManager is the source of truth for synchronized objects.
The documented key remains valid until revoked.

questions.question: Central sync works, but endpoint posture tags are absent. Which relationship is separate?

options.feedback: Local-AS is a BGP neighbor identity.
The matcher is a privileged app feature.
ACS affects SAML redirects.
Correct: ZTNA telemetry is distinct from central configuration management.

questions.question: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 rejects SAML because the IdP still signs with SHA-1. What is supported?

options.feedback: SHA-1 support has been removed; disabling validation weakens trust.
Correct: choose supported SHA-256 or SHA-512 algorithms.
RADIUS accounting does not replace SAML admin login.

options.text: Use the BGP router ID as entity ID.
options.feedback: A BGP router ID is not a SAML entity identifier.

questions.question: The IdP uses SHA-256 and the FortiAnalyzer SP uses SHA-512. Is that automatically invalid?

options.feedback: The guide allows different supported algorithms at the two ends.
SHA-1 has been removed, not required.

options.text: No; supported IdP/SP algorithm choices may differ.
options.feedback: Correct: asymmetric SAML trust permits different supported settings.
Signature validation remains part of the trust decision.

questions.question: A SAML trace shows a valid signature but a wrong ACS URL and missing RelayState. What should be fixed?

options.feedback: BGP attributes do not affect SAML browser flow.
The launcher regex is unrelated.
Local-AS is a routing attribute.
Correct: the trace points to the IdP return URL/RelayState, not signature validation.

questions.question: The SAML assertion validates, but the administrator gets the wrong ADOM. What should be inspected?

options.text: Username/profile/ADOM attribute mapping and local objects.
options.feedback: Correct: authentication can succeed while authorization maps the wrong profile or ADOM.
Duplication controls packet copies.
Radio bands do not set SAML scope.
RADIUS client matching is a separate service.

questions.question: A FortiSwitch must show a temporary AS to one peer while retaining its global ASN. Which feature fits?

options.feedback: A VDOM does not provide per-neighbor BGP identity.
Correct: local-AS is a neighbor-specific presentation; global AS remains required.

options.text: Change the router ID to the peer ASN.
options.feedback: Router ID is not an AS number.

options.text: Redistribute all connected routes into OSPF.
options.feedback: OSPF redistribution does not solve BGP peer identity.

questions.question: The BGP process will not start after local-AS is configured on a neighbor. What is still required?

options.feedback: SASE registration is unrelated.
MLO is wireless configuration.

options.text: Global BGP ASN and router ID.
options.feedback: Correct: the global BGP process still needs its ASN and router ID.
NAC VLANs do not initialize BGP.

questions.question: A peer establishes the session but rejects routes as loops. Which evidence matters?

options.feedback: SAML does not influence BGP route acceptance.
Recording does not change AS_PATH.
MLD is a wireless metric.

options.text: Advertised AS_PATH and local-AS prepend/replace behavior.
options.feedback: Correct: the peer may see its own AS or an unexpected AS sequence.

questions.question: No eBGP prefixes are learned on a FortiSwitchOS 7.2.2+ switch. Which default deserves review?

options.feedback: Correct: explicit policy may be required to learn or advertise eBGP routes.
MLO does not affect BGP.
SAML has no routing role.
RADIUS groups do not affect the switch BGP process.

questions.question: A FAP-241K MLO SSID has one active link. What should be checked first?

options.feedback: NAC serials do not control wireless association.

options.text: Firmware, radio profile, WPA3/H2E and client capability.
options.feedback: Correct: MLO requires supported firmware/radios, security and a capable client.
Backup ADOM blocks SASE registration.
SD-WAN duplication does not create Wi-Fi links.

questions.question: What is true about MLO on FAP-441K?

options.feedback: The 2.4-GHz radio on this model is not MLO capable.
The supported MLO radios are 5 and 6 GHz.

options.text: The 2.4-GHz radio is not Wi-Fi 7 MLO capable.
options.feedback: Correct: FAP-441K/443K 2.4 GHz does not support Wi-Fi 7 MLO.
Disabling 6 GHz removes a supported link.

questions.question: A K-series AP must keep MLO service through controller loss. Which VAP settings are required?

options.feedback: Standalone operation also requires local bridge and authentication.
Local bridging alone does not authenticate clients.
Open auth is not a documented MLO prerequisite.

options.text: Local standalone, local bridging and local authentication.
options.feedback: Correct: the three controls let the AP bridge/authenticate locally.

questions.question: Which output most directly shows multiple MLD links?

options.text: diagnose wpa wpad mld with num_links and link IDs.
options.feedback: Correct: the MLD diagnostic reports link count and IDs.
BGP peers do not show Wi-Fi association.
NAC serial lists are unrelated.
Admin sessions do not expose wireless links.

questions.question: A managed FortiNAC server is reachable but cannot sync after upgrade. What two gates matter?

options.feedback: Reachability is already known and does not prove authorization.

options.text: Certificate trust and allowed serial list.
options.feedback: Correct: both certificate and serial admission must pass.
RADIUS credentials do not authorize server-to-server trust.

options.text: AP radio profile and MLO flag.
options.feedback: Wireless settings do not control NAC synchronization.

questions.question: Which serials should the FortiNAC Manager allow?

options.feedback: The Manager must authorize the managed appliances.
The primary serial alone omits managed servers.
Correct: the Manager list includes all managed server serials.
FortiGate serials are not the managed-server peer list.

questions.question: An HA secondary has a stale allowlist after a change. Where should the admin normally change it?

options.feedback: Switch-port configuration does not control NAC HA state.
The secondary receives the primary configuration.
RADIUS is not the HA configuration authority.

options.text: On the primary, then verify replication.
options.feedback: Correct: make the HA change on the primary and verify the secondary.

questions.question: A recent case shows FortiNAC-OS servers missing from a CentOS Manager. Which field is high value?

options.feedback: Correct: incomplete role-specific allowed serials can block add/sync.
ToS duplication is packet forwarding.
SAML is administrator authentication.
PAM regex does not affect NAC server inventory.

questions.question: A FortiSwitch port is visible in root but not in the tenant VDOM. What is missing?

options.feedback: An ADOM is not a FortiGate port ownership control.
Correct: export the managed port into the tenant VDOM.
RADIUS groups do not transfer port ownership.
MLO capability does not affect port export.

questions.question: NAC discovers both VDOMs but assigns the wrong registration VLAN. What should be checked?

options.feedback: The IdP certificate affects SSO.
Local-AS controls BGP identity.
Correct: the tenant virtual-device mapping selects the VLAN.
PAM matching does not influence NAC placement.

questions.question: DHCP fails for a tenant endpoint. Which path should be traced?

options.feedback: GUI login does not prove DHCP reachability.
The root default route is only one part of the path.
Router ID does not explain DHCP relay.

options.text: Tenant VLAN, relay, VDOM link, routes and both policies.
options.feedback: Correct: verify the complete tenant-to-root DHCP path.

questions.question: What does the FortiNAC-F Virtualized Devices view provide?

options.text: Root and tenant VDOM objects for logical-network mapping.
options.feedback: Correct: tenant VDOMs are modeled and their logical networks map to tenant VLANs.
EAP curves belong to FAC.
The key is generated in FortiSASE.
MLO metrics are unrelated.

questions.question: An AP subnet has many NAS devices that should share one policy. Which object helps?

options.feedback: A NAC virtual device maps endpoint networks.
Correct: a client group lets the policy reference multiple NAS clients.
A launcher matcher identifies processes.
An ADOM is not a RADIUS client group.

questions.question: Two RADIUS policies match the same request. Which one wins?

options.feedback: Description length has no effect.
Creation time is not the tie-breaker.

options.text: The highest policy in the list.
options.feedback: Correct: the topmost eligible policy is selected.
IP ordering is not policy priority.

questions.question: Two client ranges overlap. Which client definition is chosen?

options.feedback: Secret age does not decide matching.
The broadest range is not preferred.
Alphabetical order is not the rule.
Correct: the most specific client range wins.

questions.question: Logs show a RADIUS daemon restart after client/policy edits. What does it indicate?

options.text: The service applied the configuration change.
options.feedback: Correct: client/policy changes are applied with a RADIUS service restart.
A restart does not prove endpoint success.
The log does not imply deletion.
RADIUS changes do not reset BGP.

questions.question: A Java app is identified by its command arguments, not its executable. Which matcher fits?

options.feedback: Default may miss the Java child process.
Correct: command-line matching can distinguish the Java application.
SAML claims map identity.
RADIUS groups classify NAS clients.

questions.question: A custom FortiPAM matcher is selected. Which controls are forced on?

options.feedback: Those are unrelated authentication settings.
Those are wireless settings.
Correct: custom matching requires process-tree monitoring and full-screen audit capture.
BGP controls do not govern launcher recording.

questions.question: A window-title regex catches unrelated applications. What is the best correction?

options.feedback: A broad wildcard increases false matches.
Disabling recording weakens the audit trail.
Default may not identify child/Java processes.
Correct: an anchored, stable pattern reduces unintended matches.

questions.question: The Java child window is absent from the recording. What should be checked?

options.feedback: Correct: both are forced for custom process matching and protect the audit trail.
OU hierarchy controls SASE registration.
Local-AS is BGP identity.
SAML digest does not affect recording.

questions.question: A full feed snapshot is imported, but old indicators remain. Which mode likely caused it?

options.feedback: Full is appropriate for a complete snapshot.
Correct: Incremental appends and can retain stale records.
TLS verification does not control replacement.
Python is the integration type.

questions.question: A feed fetch succeeds but the IOC group is empty. What boundary is next?

options.feedback: Wireless state is unrelated.
NAC trust does not affect SIEM parsing.

options.text: Normalized CSV output and AppServer parsing.
options.feedback: Correct: HTTP success does not prove valid CSV or AppServer ingestion.
VPN routing does not affect the parser.

questions.question: The feed uses a valid public certificate. What should SSL Verify do?

options.feedback: Disabling validation hides certificate problems.
Randomized verification is not meaningful.
An empty store prevents trust validation.

options.text: Remain enabled; repair trust if it fails.
options.feedback: Correct: keep TLS verification and fix the chain/hostname.

questions.question: A script emits empty CSV after timeout and Full mode clears the IOC group. What is the design flaw?

options.text: A retrieval failure looks like a valid empty snapshot.
options.feedback: Correct: fail explicitly on fetch errors so a failed run cannot replace a good snapshot.
Group-name length is not the cause.
Timezone does not make a timeout valid data.
Popup settings belong to endpoint protection.

questions.question: A PUA is detected between weekly scans. Which trigger should run a scan?

options.feedback: The schedule leaves a gap after the software change.
Correct: PUA detection is a software-change trigger event.
Logout signing affects SSO.
The key registers SASE with FMG.

questions.question: Endpoint connects and its OS updates. Which trigger covers those events?

options.feedback: Software-change is for application install/update and PUA detection.
BGP is unrelated.
Correct: event-based scanning covers connection, OS update and signature update events.
The matcher is for privileged app tracking.

questions.question: A scan finds CVEs but the endpoint remains vulnerable. What distinction matters?

options.feedback: Scanning does not install patches by itself.
A finding does not prove remediation.
A popup only notifies the user.

options.text: Scanning and automatic patching are separate actions.
options.feedback: Correct: verify the separate patch workflow and result.

questions.question: The software-change trigger is enabled but no scan follows an app update. What should be checked first?

options.text: Assigned endpoint profile and agent inventory event.
options.feedback: Correct: the endpoint must receive the profile and report the change event.
BGP ASN does not trigger endpoint scans.
NAC serials do not govern SASE profiles.
SAML digest does not trigger vulnerability scans.

questions.question: A duplication rule uses ToS 0x77 and mask 0xff. Which packet matches?

options.feedback: 0x00 does not match the configured byte.
Correct: mask 0xff compares all eight bits with 0x77.
Address family does not bypass ToS matching.

options.text: Any packet on the fastest link.
options.feedback: Link speed is not the match condition.

questions.question: The sender duplicates packets, but the server receives multiple copies. What is missing?

options.feedback: The key is for SASE management.
RADIUS groups classify NAS clients.
Correct: the receiver needs a matching rule with packet-de-duplication enabled.
MLO is unrelated to WAN copies.

questions.question: A zone has four members and duplication-max-num is 3. What does the limit mean?

options.text: Three extra copies plus the original.
options.feedback: The maximum counts member paths, not only extra copies.
BGP peer count is unrelated.
Discrepancy is a separate latency setting.

options.text: At most three member paths, original plus two copies.
options.feedback: Correct: a maximum of three means original plus two copies.

questions.question: A ToS 0x00 ping succeeds under a 0x77/0xff rule. What does it prove?

options.text: Connectivity works; the ping should not match the duplication rule.
options.feedback: Correct: a non-matching ping is a negative test; success proves connectivity only.

options.text: The duplication rule must duplicate every ping.
options.feedback: The rule is intentionally selective.
No multiple-copy evidence exists.
A rewrite must not be assumed without a marking policy.

questions.question: Which statement separates Wi-Fi MLO from SD-WAN duplication?

options.feedback: Local-AS is a routing identity feature.

options.text: MLO uses multiple wireless links in one association; duplication copies IP packets across WAN members.
options.feedback: Correct: MLO is a wireless multi-link association; SD-WAN duplicates packets across paths.

options.text: Both are enabled with a ToS mask.
options.feedback: ToS masks select duplicated IP traffic only.
NAC serials authorize FortiNAC peers only.

questions.question: A tenant host has the right VLAN but cannot reach FortiNAC. Which path is most relevant?

options.feedback: SAML admin login is unrelated to host reachability.
Process tracking is a PAM audit feature.

options.text: Tenant-to-root VDOM link, routes, policies and DHCP relay.
options.feedback: Correct: tenant traffic to FortiNAC traverses the VDOM link and root-side policy/routing path.
Local-AS is not the primary NAC tenant path check.
